run.question: List the top 5 largest Elasticsearch indices matching the pattern 'app-184-*' by document count. Show their names and doc counts.

report.summary: Queried the Elasticsearch source otel-demo for indices matching 'app-184-*' sorted by docs.count descending. The first call exceeded the return limit, so I read the head of the stored result (offset 0, limit 10), which is the top of the descending sort. The five largest indices each hold 500 documents: app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25 (500, 45.7kb, green), app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10 (500, 44.7kb, green), app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20 (500, 31kb, green), app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 (500, 46.8kb, green) and app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15 (500, 30kb, green). The next rows in the same slice drop to 1 document, so 500 documents is the maximum observed and the drop to the remaining indices is sharp. The ranking answer is therefore supported; the read slice is truncated at 10 of 1800 rows and the listing carries no time range, so no totals or window-specific statements are made.

claims.text: The read slice of the app-184-* index listing sorted by docs.count descending shows app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25 with docs.count 500, store.size 45.7kb, health green.

The same slice shows four more indices at the 500-document level: app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10 (500 docs, 44.7kb, green), app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20 (500 docs, 31kb, green), app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 (500 docs, 46.8kb, green) and app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15 (500 docs, 30kb, green).

Rows six through ten of the same descending slice (app-184-ml-billing-2024.01.09, app-184-data-db-2024.01.34, app-184-ml-billing-2024.01.08, app-184-data-db-2024.01.35, app-184-ml-billing-2024.01.07) each show docs.count 1 and health green, so document counts drop from 500 to 1 immediately below the top five.

gaps: The only delivered view is a truncated slice: 10 of 1800 rows were read (offset 0, limit 10). Rows 10-1799 and the total/minimum counts are unknown; no sum or complete distribution can be stated.

The earlier listing call returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE with status error and is not citable; that it matched 1800 indices and exceeded the token limit is recorded here as a limit of the Run, not as a fact claim, and no breakdown of its contents is asserted.

The index listing carries no time range (source_start_at and source_end_at are null), so these document counts are only as of the query and are not tied to the authorized window 2026-11-21T10:22:18Z to 2026-11-22T10:22:18Z.
Ordering among the five 500-document indices reflects the backend's tie ordering, not a difference in size; all five share the same document count.
Change history is not integrated, so whether any of these indices were created or altered during the window could not be checked.
next_steps: If a complete ranking or a breakdown below the top five is needed, page the stored result in slices of roughly 700 rows, or re-query with narrower patterns such as app-184-ml-* or app-184-data-*.
